new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no prior statement for Mand (our earlier reading found nothing in Daniels 2015 or Z'graggen). This adds the only placement statement that exists, but at the level of the Sogeram family, with Mand/Atemple included only nominally and on stress-less wordlist data.
new_statements.rule_in_words: A one-sentence family-level statement: word stress is almost always on the final syllable in the Sogeram daughter languages, and Proto-Sogeram probably had final stress too. There is no Atemple/Mand-specific statement; Atemple appears only in the classification (fig. 1 p. 165), the West Sogeram discussion (p. 172) and sec. 3.2 'Atemple innovations' (pp. 173-174), which give a tentative phoneme chart from Z'graggen's phonetic transcriptions and two sound changes (nasal deletion, sporadic m-fortition) and say nothing about stress. Daniels states (p. 165) that the Atemple data come from Z'graggen's (1980d) wordlist, which itself omits stress marks, so the 'daughter languages' claim cannot rest on Atemple data; his own field data in 2010 cover Nend, Manat, Mum, Sirva, Aisi, Kulsab.
new_statements.exceptions: The hedge 'almost always' is not expanded; no exceptions or conditions are listed.
new_statements.identity_note: Both works are about the same language: Daniels 2010 calls it 'Atemple' (Z'graggen's village name; Atemble/Atemble-Apris elsewhere), spoken by 65 people in one village at Z'graggen's survey and reported 'no longer spoken' by PBT staff in 2010 (p. 172); Daniels 2020 calls it 'Mand' (the word for 'no'), one village on the Ramu, eight remaining speakers (p. 2; Table 1 p. 4 equates Mand with Atemple). Daniels' own Mand fieldwork was 2-3 weeks in 2011-12 and two weeks in 2014 (2020 p. 11). No dialects are distinguished.

readall_conflicts: No outright contradiction, but a tension in the author's own statements across time: Daniels 2010 (p. 168) asserts that stress is almost always word-final in the Sogeram daughter languages and probably was in Proto-Sogeram, whereas Daniels 2015 (p. 72) and 2020 (p. 60), writing after his own Mand fieldwork (2011-12, 2014), say only that 'further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern' and drop the Proto-Sogeram stress claim from the phonology chapter; in 2020 word-final stress is asserted only for Manat (p. 65). For Mand the 2010 claim rests on no Mand data (Atemple data there are Z'graggen's stress-less wordlist), so the final-stress reading for Mand is a family-level inference, not a description.

sources.note: Nothing on where Mand stress falls. Phonology sec. 1.2 (pp. 443-447) covers consonants, vowels, allophony of /a/ /z/ and prenasalized stops, status of /w y ɨ/, vowel elision; no word stress, accent or tone. Only remark: sec. 2.2.2.3 p. 72 (PDF p. 97) 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.' Whole-text search for stress/accent/tone/prosody: no other word-level hit.
Nothing; speaker numbers (8 fluent speakers in 2014), fieldwork dates, contact history only.
